amendments.body: In `nitrogen_cycle.rs`, the `monod_rate` helper now receives concentration-based substrate values but its doc comment and parameter name (`substrate`) give no indication of expected units. Add a brief doc comment to `monod_rate` and `monod_factor` noting that `substrate` and `k_substrate` must be in the same units (mg/L after the concentration migration) so future maintainers don't accidentally pass totals.
amendments.rationale: The function previously implicitly worked with totals; now it implicitly works with concentrations. Since it's a private helper, the risk is low, but the same function is called with `concentration_from_total(do_budget, volume_l)` (an ad-hoc local concentration) AND with `state.water.tan_mg_n_per_l(volume_l)` (a canonical helper). A comment prevents someone from passing raw totals in the future.

amendments.body: The `substrate_displacement_l` function in `geometry.rs` assumes 0% substrate porosity — the entire substrate volume is subtracted from water volume. Real aquarium substrates have ~30-40% porosity, so 60-70% of the substrate column is solid. Consider adding a `porosity_index` field to `SubstrateKind` or `SubstrateLayerState` and multiplying displacement by `(1.0 - porosity)`. At minimum, add a doc comment noting the 100% displacement assumption so dependents (especially the `water_volume_l_with_substrate_depth` callers) are aware.
amendments.rationale: This affects every concentration computation in the simulation. For a 2cm substrate in a 12cm fill height, the model removes 16.7% of water volume when the real displacement is ~10-12%. Over-subtraction inflates all dissolved concentrations by a corresponding factor, which compounds through Monod kinetics across every system. Since concentration accuracy is the central goal of this bead, the assumption should at least be documented.

amendments.body: The `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l` and `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_m2` conversion functions use hardcoded reference constants (20 L, 0.1 m²). If the default tank geometry changes, these constants silently become wrong. Add a compile-time assertion or comment linking these constants to the `TankGeometry::default()` values to prevent silent divergence.
amendments.rationale: The constants `LEGACY_KINETIC_REFERENCE_VOLUME_L = 20.0` and `LEGACY_KINETIC_REFERENCE_FOOTPRINT_M2 = 0.1` are derived from the default geometry (40×25×22 cm), but this relationship is implicit. The default geometry has `fill_height_cm: 22.0` and default substrate `depth_cm: 2.0`, yielding 20 L net volume only if substrate displacement is `footprint * 2cm / 1000 = 2.0 L`, leaving `22-2=20 L`. If anyone changes the default geometry or substrate, the reference constants become inconsistent and all legacy param conversions silently break.

payload.summary: Reviewed the full changeset implementing canonical concentration helpers and compartment APIs (tanksim-6e5.2.2). All 116 tests pass. The implementation is well-structured: `concentration_from_total` is the single canonical division point with proper zero-volume and NaN guards; `ConcentrationView` provides a borrow-based view avoiding repeated volume calculations; all process systems (nitrogen cycle, plant growth, algae growth, shrimp, events, dissolved oxygen, chemistry, snapshot) have been migrated from raw `total / geometry.water_volume_l()` to the new helpers using net water volume. The schema v2→v3 migration correctly rescales dissolved totals from gross to net volume. The `ProcessParams` struct has `#[serde(default)]` so the new `decomposer_k_do_mg` field deserializes safely from old saves. The proptest verifies non-negativity across random geometry/chemistry inputs. The `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l` bridge for the Monod half-saturation constants is mathematically correct for the 20 L reference tank. Three amendments proposed: (1) document units on `monod_rate`/`monod_factor` to prevent future regressions, (2) the 0% porosity substrate displacement model over-subtracts water volume which inflates all concentrations — at minimum document the assumption, (3) the legacy reference constants are silently coupled to default geometry and could diverge.
